why: In Denmark, using a Rejsekort on public transport is universally referred to as 'checking in' (at checke ind). Using the word 'scans' in the English summary might lead the generator to produce a literal but unnatural translation like 'scanner mit rejsekort'.

Software companies in Denmark typically use a subsidized monthly 'kantineordning' (canteen scheme/buffet) deducted from salary, rather than having employees pay cash at a register for individual items like a single smørrebrød. While fine for practicing prices, it's slightly un-Danish for this specific work setting.

issue: Relies on an abstract feeling to resolve the scene instead of a concrete action.
why: Ending the scene with 'feels happy and completely at home' acts as a static emotional inventory. Grounding this transition with a concrete physical action (like checking her mailbox, hanging up her keys, or taking off her coat) would maintain the active, sensory texture of the rest of the week.

Both scenes resolve with almost the exact same mechanical action ('and pays fyrre kroner at the register' / 'and pays femogtres kroner to the smiling baker'). It feels a little formulaic so close together; varying the phrasing for one of the purchases would make it feel more natural.

Both Scenes 4 and 6 resolve with the exact same structural beat: Maya orders a food item and explicitly 'pays [spelled-out number] kroner'. Omitting the explicit payment in one of them (e.g., just receiving the boxed cake with a smile) would make the narrative less formulaic while still reviewing shop vocabulary.
